content.summary: Change is small, additive and well-tested. Expiry is enforced in one place (LinkService.resolve) and inherited by both read paths; stats intentionally bypass it. Migration is additive and idempotent with upgrade tests against a v1 database. The only protected-file change (ApiExceptionHandler) is a single switch case.

findings.issue: validateExpiry runs after the idempotency short-circuit, so a replayed request with a now-past expiresAt still returns the original link.
findings.recommendation: Intended: idempotent replays must return the original outcome. Document it.

findings.issue: Migrations are hand-rolled inside the repository.
findings.recommendation: Fine at v2; move to Flyway before v4.
Inject a Clock bean override for integration tests to remove wall-clock waits.
Diff reviewed: `case GONE, EXPIRED -> HttpStatus.GONE`. No handler logic changed. Approved via policy:implement:T3 checkpoint.

policySummary: path-allowlist blocked a stray .env.local in T2 attempt 1 (retry succeeded)
protected-files-require-approval raised on T3 attempt 2 and was approved by the reviewer
